_doc: Rival railroad barons (all fictional), their personalities, and the rules for mergers, board votes and bankruptcy. See BALANCING.md.

builder.name: Cautious builder
builder.desc: Builds solid lines between big towns, keeps cash in reserve, avoids debt, pays dividends.

expander.name: Aggressive expander
expander.desc: Builds fast and far on borrowed money, crowds into served towns and swallows weak rivals.

speculator.name: Stock speculator
speculator.desc: Builds a little, trades a lot: buys cheap shares, sells short what looks dear and raids weak railroads.

merger._doc: A baron holding at least minStake of a company may propose merging it into the company he chairs. Target shareholders get acquirer shares worth the target price plus `premium`. Votes: the proposer's shares yes, the target's chairman no, other barons yes, the public yes with publicBase + premium x publicPerPremium (+ badYearBonus if the target's share price fell this year). More than half carries it.

board._doc: Each January from the third year on, the shareholders of your company vote on you: your shares for you, the public with publicBase + perPriceChange x share-price change over the year + profitBonus (or - lossPenalty), rival barons against you unless rivals are friendly. Below half is a vote of no confidence; two in a row and you are out.

bankruptcy._doc: A company whose debts exceed its assets cannot borrow; if its cash is still negative after monthsInsolvent month-ends it goes bankrupt: its shares become worthless and its railway is torn up.
